papers.title_en: What Attention Recalls and Recurrence Controls in Hybrid Language Models
papers.authors: Kirill Afendulev, Alexey Dontsov, Elena Tutubalina, Anton Korznikov
papers.evidence: 对混合注意力和循环语言模型做缓存级干预，区分精确检索与输出语言控制功能
papers.tldr: 混合语言模型将注意力与固定大小的循环状态结合，但两种通道的功能分工未知。本文提出分割预填充与状态交换两种干预，分别隔离或错配KV缓存与循环状态。在Qwen3.5和Falcon-H1上发现清晰分工：精确检索仅依赖注意力，语言风格和人格主要依赖循环状态。因果验证表明答案值来自注意力侧，语言由循环状态决定。
papers.abstract_en: Hybrid language models combine attention with a fixed-size recurrent state, but the role of each channel remains unclear. We introduce two cache-level interventions. Split-prefill keeps only the KV cache or only the recurrent state from a prefilled context, then generates an answer. State-swap pairs the KV cache from one context with the recurrent state from another in a single forward pass. On Qwen3.5 and Falcon-H1, the two channels split sharply by function. Exact retrieval survives only through attention (64-98% of full accuracy) and collapses to zero through recurrence. Output language and persona reverse the pattern: both survive recurrence (70-80% and 3-5x) while KV-only drops to ~1% language accuracy. State-swap confirms this causally: the answer takes its value from the KV side and its language from the recurrent side. Recurrent-only generation also accepts words that were never in the context but share meaning or parts with seen items. Attention provides a lookup over what was said; the recurrent state shapes how the model says it next.

papers.title_en: HitMem: Hierarchical Temporal 3D Memory with Multi-Modal Context-Aware Retrieval for Dynamic Environments
papers.authors: Ruijie Tang, Chenye Zou, Guoquan Wu, Jun Wei, Wei Chen, Jiaxin Zhu
papers.evidence: 动态场景中的层级时态三维记忆与多模态检索，接近记忆增强神经网络方向
papers.tldr: 动态环境中物体易被移动，现有基于静态假设的三维记忆导致记忆与观察冲突且需昂贵重计算。为此提出HitMem，通过持续感知构建统一语义与空间信息的层次拓扑图，并利用时间衰减动态调节记忆活跃度。其多模态上下文感知检索在检测到位移时，结合轨迹空间约束与类别语义常识进行两阶段定位。在Dyna-THOR上显著提升物体重定位准确率并降低探索开销，为长期任务在动态环境中的执行提供可靠记忆支撑。
papers.abstract_en: Executing long-term tasks in dynamic environments requires embodied agents to maintain robust and adaptive 3D scene representations. However, most existing 3D memory frameworks rely on static world assumptions. When objects are displaced by human activities or unobserved events, agents encounter memory-observation conflicts and often require costly geometric recomputations or inefficient global re-exploration. To address this, we propose HitMem, a hierarchical temporal 3D memory framework with a multi-modal context-aware retrieval mechanism. Through continuous perception, HitMem unifies semantic and spatial information into a lightweight topological graph that captures support relationships, while a temporal decay mechanism dynamically regulates memory activeness to mitigate the impact of stale representations. In addition, the multi-modal context-aware retrieval mechanism defaults to filtering candidates using integrated semantic, spatial, and temporal memory features, and activates a specialized two-stage retrieval process when object displacement is detected. This process combines spatial constraints inferred from external agent trajectories with semantic common sense grounded in class affinities, efficiently identifying high-probability candidate regions. Extensive evaluations on our constructed Dyna-THOR benchmark demonstrate that HitMem significantly improves object relocation accuracy, reduces exploration costs, and enhances task execution performance in dynamic environments.

papers.title_en: LookStep: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation with Linguistic Foresight and Event Driven Memory
papers.authors: Kun-Yang Yu, Yingzhe Li, Hongyu Xu, Shi-Yu Tian, Zhi Zhou, Yang Chen, Ming Yang, Sheng Wang, Qing Yu, Lan-Zhe Guo, Yu-Feng Li
papers.evidence: 提出事件驱动滚动记忆和语言中心未来状态建模，面向记忆增强的高效视觉语言导航
papers.tldr: 视觉语言导航要求智能体在未知环境遵循指令。现有MLLM方法采用下一步动作预测范式，仅监督专家动作，数据需求高且依赖地图或历史帧，开销大。为此提出LookStep，一个统一端到端框架，包含语言中心未来状态建模和事件驱动滚动记忆，用语言标签为候选动作生成粗粒度导航进程与未来状态，并自动决定是否写入有界记忆。在VLN-CE上，LookStep以更少数据和更好内存效率取得R2R-CE Val-Unseen 49.7%成功率，优于同设置方法。
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow natural-language instructions in unseen environments. Recent progress has been largely driven by Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Existing methods follow a next-step action prediction paradigm, supervising only the expert action, which requires a high quantity of data for training. They also rely on cognitive maps, accumulated historical frames, or external 3D tools to maintain states, leading to high computational and memory overhead. To realize resource efficiency VLN, we propose LookStep, a unified end-to-end framework that combines Language Centric Future State Modeling and Event Driven Rolling Memory that uses language labels to generate coarse-grained navigation progress and future states for each candidate action, while autonomously deciding whether to write each observation into a bounded rolling memory with a semantic role. We validate LookStep empirically. On VLN-CE tasks, LookStep outperforms existing methods under the same training settings, achieving a 49.7\% success rate on R2R-CE Val-Unseen with better memory efficiency and less data usage. Code and model is available at https://github.com/kunyang-YU/LookStep.
